title: Customers whose latest order beat their first
statementMd:
Among customers with at least 2 non-cancelled orders, list those whose latest order total (by date, then id) is larger than their first order total. Show customer name.

Expected columns: `name`.

Tables: `customers`, `products`, `orders`, `order_items`.

Row order does not matter.
hints: `FIRST_VALUE` with ascending and descending windows over order totals.
solutionMd:
```sql
WITH t AS (SELECT o.customer_id, o.id, o.order_date, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY o.id), r AS (SELECT *, FIRST_VALUE(total) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date, id) AS first_total, FIRST_VALUE(total) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC, id DESC) AS last_total, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS n FROM t) SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM r JOIN customers c ON c.id = r.customer_id WHERE n >= 2 AND last_total > first_total;
```

Compare with your own query; the result sets must match.
